title: Cybersecurity as a career
description: Principles, real roles, and how to keep advancing.

1.title: The professional's principles and the role map
1.body:
## CIA: the goal of everything

**Confidentiality** (only those who should, see), **Integrity** (data is not altered
without authorization), **Availability** (the system is there when it's needed). Every
security control protects one of the three. Add authentication and non-repudiation
to get the five-element model (AAA).

## The role map (the ones you can already recognize)

| Role | Does | Keywords |
|---|---|---|
| **Pentester** | authorized attacks + report | the commercial "red team" |
| **Red teamer** | simulates real adversaries, stealth | TTPs, evasion |
| **SOC analyst** | monitors and responds | SIEM, triage (your module 10) |
| **DFIR** | forensics + incident response | evidence, timeline |
| **Threat hunter** | searches for what the alerts didn't see | hypothesis, anomaly |
| **AppSec / DevSecOps** | security in the code and the pipeline | SDLC, SAST/DAST |
| **GRC** | standards, risk, audit | ISO 27001, NIST |

None of them is "better": they are perspectives on the same problem. Yours starts with the one
that hooked you the most in this path.

ciberseguridad-como-carrera-t01-q01.prompt: Which of these is the classic information security triad?
ciberseguridad-como-carrera-t01-q01.hint: Three words starting with C, I and A.

ciberseguridad-como-carrera-t01-q02.prompt: Which role is dedicated to breaking systems WITH AUTHORIZATION to find flaws?
ciberseguridad-como-carrera-t01-q02.hint: The one you've been learning in the offensive half of the path.

ciberseguridad-como-carrera-t01-q03.prompt: A colleague asks you to 'test' their company's website without written permission. What do you do as a professional?

options.b: Refuse until you have written authorization (scope) from someone in charge
options.c: Test just a little, without causing damage

2.title: How to keep going from here
2.body:
## The route that works

1. **Practice in public**: solve labs and WRITE your own write-ups (GitHub/ blog).
   A clear write-up is worth more than ten certificates on your CV.
2. **Build**: a home lab (you already have one: CyberArena!), your own scripts — this
   very platform is a portfolio project.
3. **Go deeper**: this platform's **Jr Penetration Tester** path continues
   exactly where you are: Nmap, Burp, privilege escalation, Active Directory,
   with dedicated Docker labs.
4. **Specialize later**: Offensive (PT2/Web/Red Team), Defensive (SOC/DFIR) or
   AppSec. The specialist's T is built on a general base — and this IS your base.

## The habits of good professionals

- **Read everything**: advisories, other people's write-ups, changelogs. Curiosity is the
  number one skill in the field.
- **Impeccable ethics**: your reputation is your most fragile asset. Written authorization,
  always, for everything.
- **Share**: the community (CTFs, write-ups, mentoring) is how everyone you admire today
  grew.

**Congratulations**: you have finished Cyber Security 101. Go to your dashboard,
check your level and your badges… and when you're ready: we'll be waiting for you in Jr Penetration
Tester. 🚩

ciberseguridad-como-carrera-t02-q01.prompt: What demonstrates MORE real capability in a cybersecurity job interview?
ciberseguridad-como-carrera-t02-q01.hint: What you have DONE, not what you say you know.

options.a: An expensive certificate with no practice
options.b: Solved labs, your own write-ups and a portfolio of projects

ciberseguridad-como-carrera-t02-q02.prompt: On this platform, which path comes next after Cyber Security 101?
ciberseguridad-como-carrera-t02-q02.hint: The name of this very site gives you a clue… it's the junior pentesting one.
